```{r}
#| include: false
qc_metrics <- read.csv("qc_symptom_metrics.csv", check.names = FALSE)
d <- readRDS("qc_gallery_examples.rds")
fmt <- function(x, digits = 3) formatC(x, digits = digits, format = "f")
```

## Overview

When an end-to-end single-trial fMRI analysis yields unexpectedly weak slopes, implausibly shifted peri-event peaks, or inflated connectivity estimates, identifying *which pipeline stage* introduced the distortion is much faster when you know the visual signature each failure mode leaves behind. Because MEDuSA preserves explicit diagnostic summaries, operator resolution metrics, and propagated standard errors at every stage (see the [end-to-end data-flow schematic](../foundations.qmd#fig-pipeline-dataflow)), most upstream mis-specifications can be localized in a few lines of R before fitting group models across hundreds of parcels.

The snippet below collects the six fastest pre-flight checks across a completed or pilot participant workflow:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# 1. Step 0: Check motion censoring share, dummy frames, and event clock bounds (in seconds)
print(sub01$confounds$summary[, c("run", "n_volumes", "pct_censored", "n_non_steady_state")])
lapply(split(sub01$events$onset, sub01$events$run), range)

# 2. Step 1: Check out-of-sample HRF task relevance and AR(p) rho stationarity ceiling (0.90)
lapply(hrf_fit$selections, function(s) summary(s$selected_task_p))
lapply(hrf_fit$noise, function(n) quantile(n$rho[, 1], probs = c(0.5, 0.9, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE))

# 3. Step 2: Check deconvolution conditional self-gain and attenuation
diagnose_crossrun_recovery(decon, events = sub01$events)$summary

# 4. Step 3 & 4: Audit trial-level SE distribution and BOLD-coverage NA gating
summary(epochs$panel$se_demixed)
mean(is.na(epochs$panel$decon_demixed))

# 5. Step 5: Verify predictor centering (run/person mean ~ 0) and random-effect singularity
tapply(group_panel$rpe_within, group_panel$id, mean, na.rm = TRUE) |> summary()

# 6. Step 6: Inspect M-MOMS attenuation factor (alpha_final) and shared cross-parcel error
summary(ppi$subjects[, c("estimate", "r_shared_error", "alpha_final", "converged")])
```

::: {.callout-note}
### How to Use This Gallery
Each section below pairs a **healthy MEDuSA run** (blue) against one or two **realistic mis-specifications** (red/amber) generated on the same underlying neural ground truth using `medusa`. Start with the lookup table in the next section to match an observed symptom to its pipeline stage, then jump to the corresponding visual pair for the diagnostic check and remedy.
:::

## Quick Symptom-to-Remedy Reference

| Observed symptom | Field or plot to inspect | Underlying mechanism | Recommended remedy |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Peri-event curve peaks several seconds *before* `0 s` (e.g., at `-4 s` or `-6 s`) | `decon_epoch_regression(..., lags = -6:6)` lag profile | Initial dummy volumes were physically dropped from the 4D NIfTI while `events$onset` stayed referenced to scanner trigger `t = 0` (`time_offset = 0`) | Keep full 4D runs and mask dummy frames via `valid_rows` (`include_non_steady_state = TRUE`), or set `time_offset = k * tr` ([Step 0](../medusa_step0_design_bids/medusa_step0_design_bids.qmd)) |
| Task slopes attenuate under task-correlated motion, or `noise_sd` stays elevated after ICA-AROMA | `sub01$aroma$summary` & `decon$scaling[[r]]$noise_sd` | Aggressive AROMA stripped shared task-motion variance (Pruim et al., 2015), or uncleaned `csf`/`white_matter` confounds re-injected removed motion ICs during Step 1–2 nuisance projection (Lindquist et al., 2019) | Use `aroma = "nonaggressive"` with `aroma_clean_nuisance = TRUE` and `strategy = "csf_wm"` ([Step 0 §0.5](../medusa_step0_design_bids/medusa_step0_design_bids.qmd#sec-nonaggressive-aroma)) |
| Virtually all parcels fail Step 1 task screening (`selected_task_p > 0.10`) and lag-0 slopes vanish | `range(events$onset)` vs. `(nrow(Y) - 1) * tr` | Event onsets were supplied in **TR indices** (or milliseconds) rather than physical **seconds**, compressing or stretching the forward design | Convert `onset` and `duration` to seconds before calling `estimate_crossrun_hrf()` ([Step 0](../medusa_step0_design_bids/medusa_step0_design_bids.qmd)) |
| Large fraction of parcels/voxels pile up at `rho = 0.90` in Step 1 | Histogram of `hrf_fit$noise[[r]]$rho[, 1]` | Unmodeled scanner shim shifts, low-frequency drift, or respiratory alias forces $\text{AR}(1)$ autocorrelation onto its stationarity upper bound | Include cosine/polynomial drift (`drift_order = 2` or `fMRIPrep` cosines), mask motion spikes via `valid_rows`, and use `motion_bandstop_bpm` for fast-TR runs ([Step 1](../medusa_step1_hrf_noise/medusa_step1_hrf_noise.qmd)) |
| Deconvolved time series $\widehat{a}_r(t)$ looks overly flat and Step 3 peaks are blunted | `diagnose_crossrun_recovery(decon, events)$summary$mean_gain` | Penalty $\lambda_v$ was fixed too high (e.g., manual override), collapsing conditional self-gain toward zero | Leave `lambda = NULL` so Step 2 tunes $\lambda_v$ automatically per series via GCV/REML ([Step 2](../medusa_step2_deconvolution/medusa_step2_deconvolution.qmd)) |
| Sharp positive/negative ringing lobes appear $\pm 6\text{--}10\text{ s}$ around isolated frames | Continuous trace `decon$deconvolved[[r]]` overlaid on `confounds` FD | Uncensored head-motion or coil spike with `rwls = "none"` rings through the inverse Toeplitz filter $D_r$ | Pass FD censor mask via `valid_rows` and keep adaptive `rwls = "auto"` enabled in Step 2 ([Step 2](../medusa_step2_deconvolution/medusa_step2_deconvolution.qmd)) |
| Individual trials show sharp `se_demixed` spikes or `NA` estimates | Trial index vs. `panel$se_demixed` and `is.na(panel$decon_demixed)` | Censoring inside a trial's causal HRF window reduces Fisher information (elevating `se_demixed`) or drops BOLD support below `min_bold_coverage` (`NA`) | Expected protective behavior: retain `precision_weight_cohort` so noisy trials are downweighted automatically; exclude entire runs only when censoring is pervasive (`> 25–30%`) ([Step 3](../medusa_step3_epochs/medusa_step3_epochs.qmd)) |
| Group fixed-effect slopes in Step 5 appear ~30–60% smaller than expected | Model formula outcome column (`decon_eb` vs. `decon_demixed`) | Empirical-Bayes shrunken `decon_eb` was entered as a regression outcome, shrinking group slopes by the trial reliability factor | Always enter `decon_demixed` + `weights = "precision_weight_cohort"` when neural activity is the outcome; reserve `decon_eb` for visualization or standalone predictor summaries ([Step 4](../medusa_step4_parcel_panels/medusa_step4_parcel_panels.qmd)) |
| Step 5 slope flips sign or has `df` in the thousands; Step 6 connectivity is inflated or attenuated | Step 5 formula & `df`; Step 6 `ppi$subjects$r_shared_error` | Uncentered `x_raw` conflates trait and state slopes; omitting `(1 + x_within || id)` treats trials as independent; stripping `unit_error_cor` (`shared_error = "zero"`) disattenuates shared noise | Center predictors within person/run and include random slopes in Step 5 ([Step 5](../medusa_step5_group_models/medusa_step5_group_models.qmd)); preserve `subject_epochs` metadata and keep `shared_error = "auto"` with `method = "mmoms"` in Step 6 ([Step 6](../medusa_step6_connectivity/medusa_step6_connectivity.qmd)) |

@tbl-qc-summary summarizes the quantitative contrast between the healthy baseline and the mis-specified pipeline in each simulated benchmark shown below.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-qc-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Healthy versus mis-specified diagnostic benchmarks across Steps 0–6 (generated live via simulate_qc_gallery.R)."
#| echo: false
knitr::kable(
  qc_metrics,
  col.names = c("Pipeline Stage & Diagnostic Contrast", "Healthy Signature", "Mis-Specified Signature"),
  align = c("l", "l", "l")
)
```

## Visual Diagnostic Pairs Across the Pipeline

### 1. Steps 0 & 1: Event-Clock Shifts, Onset-Unit Errors, and AR(1) Ceiling Pile-Ups {#sec-qc-step01}

![Healthy versus mis-specified diagnostics in Steps 0 and 1. **A:** True feedback RPE slope (`0.60` at lag `0 s`, `TR = 2.0 s`) recovered cleanly when initial dummy volumes are masked via `valid_rows` (blue), versus physically dropping 3 dummy volumes without setting `time_offset = 6` (solid red, shifting the recovered peak backward to `-6 s`) or supplying `events$onset` in TR indices rather than seconds (dashed amber, compressing all events into the first half of the scan and destroying the association). **B:** Parcel-level `hrf_fit$noise$run1$rho` across 36 parcels (true $\rho \in [0.30, 0.62]$) on detrended BOLD (blue) versus BOLD contaminated by an unmodeled mid-run shim step and low-frequency drift (red, pinning 100% of parcels against the `0.90` stationarity ceiling).](figures/01-qc-clock-and-rho.png){#fig-qc-step01 width="100%" fig-alt="Two-panel diagnostic comparison for Steps 0 and 1 showing backward-shifted or flattened peri-event lag curves from clock/unit bugs on the left, and AR(1) rho histogram pile-up at the 0.90 ceiling from unmodeled drift on the right."}

**What to look for in @fig-qc-step01:**

- **Event-clock shifts (Panel A, solid red):** If an external script slices $k$ initial dummy volumes out of the 4D NIfTI file (`Y <- Y[-c(1:k), ]`) while `events.tsv` remains referenced to the first scanner trigger (`time_offset = 0`), row 1 of the matrix is actually acquired at $t = k \cdot \text{TR}$ rather than $t = 0$. Every neural response then appears in the BOLD record $k \cdot \text{TR}$ seconds *earlier* than the event table expects—producing an unmistakable "pre-stimulus" peak at $-k \cdot \text{TR}$ (`-6 s` here for 3 dropped `2.0 s` volumes) and near-zero effect at `0 s`.
- **Onset-unit mismatches (Panel A, dashed amber):** Passing 0-based or 1-based volume indices instead of seconds when $\text{TR} \ne 1.0\text{ s}$ rescales the entire task timeline by $1 / \text{TR}$. Step 1's cross-run HRF selector finds almost no out-of-sample variance explained (`selected_task_p` shifts toward uniform noise), and Step 3 lag profiles flatten to zero.
- **Stationarity ceiling pile-ups (Panel B, red):** Step 1 bounds REML $\text{AR}(p)$ roots inside a causal, stationary region (`rho <= 0.90` for $\text{AR}(1)$) so prewhitening stays invertible. A natural physiological distribution spans roughly `0.25–0.70` depending on $\text{TR}$. When a large share of parcels stacks directly on `0.90`, the noise model is absorbing deterministic low-frequency drift, coil/shim jumps, or unmasked motion bursts rather than stationary innovations.

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# Diagnostic check & remedy for Steps 0-1
stopifnot(max(sub01$events$onset) <= max(sub01$confounds$summary$n_volumes) * sub01$tr)
mean(hrf_fit$noise$run1$rho[, 1] >= 0.89, na.rm = TRUE)  # healthy: typically < 0.05

# Remedy: keep intact 4D runs + valid_rows, and ensure drift + FD censoring are active
sub01   <- read_fmriprep_subject(..., strategy = "24p", fd_threshold = 0.5, include_non_steady_state = TRUE)
hrf_fit <- estimate_crossrun_hrf(sub01, kernel_grid = candidates, drift_order = 2L, pooling = "parcel")
```

For full walkthroughs of clock-preserving ingestion and prewhitening choices, see [Step 0](../medusa_step0_design_bids/medusa_step0_design_bids.qmd) and [Step 1](../medusa_step1_hrf_noise/medusa_step1_hrf_noise.qmd).

### 2. Step 2: Over-Smoothing Gain Collapse and Uncensored Spike Ringing {#sec-qc-step2}

![Healthy versus mis-specified continuous deconvolution in Step 2. **A:** Continuous restored activity trace $\widehat{a}_r(t)$ across `67–117 s` of Run 1 containing two true neural events (`76 s` and `108 s`, green dotted lines) and a framewise motion artifact at `91 s` (red dashed line). Healthy deconvolution with `valid_rows` censoring and automatic $\lambda_v$ / RWLS recovers crisp phasic peaks at `76 s` and `108 s` while suppressing `91 s` (blue). Fixing `lambda = 8.0` flattens true neural peaks nearly to zero (amber), whereas leaving the `91 s` spike uncensored with `rwls = "none"` produces strong positive and negative deconvolution ringing lobes across `82–96 s` (red). **B:** `diagnose_crossrun_recovery()` immediately flags over-smoothing via collapsed `mean_gain` (`0.043` vs. `0.317`), whereas uncensored spike artifacts leave deterministic operator `mean_gain` almost unchanged (`0.300`) and therefore require inspecting censoring masks or RWLS weights.](figures/02-qc-decon-gain-and-spikes.png){#fig-qc-step2 width="100%" fig-alt="Two-panel Step 2 diagnostic plot showing continuous deconvolved activity traces with over-smoothing vs spike ringing on the left, and diagnose_crossrun_recovery self-gain lollipops on the right."}

**What to look for in @fig-qc-step2:**

- **Gain collapse from over-regularization (amber):** Because continuous deconvolution trades variance reduction against temporal shrinkage via the resolution matrix $D_r H_r$, setting `lambda` manually to a large value crushes the diagonal self-gain of `diagnose_crossrun_recovery()` below `0.05`. Notice that `deconvolve_crossrun_hrf()` scales penalties cleanly when `scaling = "noise_sd"` and `lambda = NULL`; manual `lambda` overrides are rarely needed outside sensitivity analyses.
- **Why spike ringing requires *both* operator and residual/weight checks (red):** Look closely at Panel B: the uncensored spike run (`rwls = "none"`, no `valid_rows` mask) still reports a healthy-looking `mean_gain = 0.300` in `diagnose_crossrun_recovery()`. That is because `mean_gain` audits the *linear operator* $D_r H_r$, which depends on the HRF, run schedule, and $\lambda_v$—not on an isolated BOLD outlier in $y_r$. An unmasked motion spike acts like a delta impulse that does *not* follow the slow hemodynamic shape $h_r$; inverting $H_r$ therefore surrounds the spike with alternating positive and negative side-lobes across neighboring timepoints. Masking high-FD frames via `valid_rows` (Step 0) and keeping `rwls = "auto"` (Step 2) prevents these artifacts from contaminating nearby trials.

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# Check both operator gain AND adaptive RWLS outlier downweighting
rec <- diagnose_crossrun_recovery(decon, events = sub01$events)
print(rec$summary[, c("run", "mean_gain", "mean_abs_gain_error", "mean_abs_excess_leakage")])

# Inspect minimum RWLS observation weights per run (weights << 1 indicate downweighted residual spikes)
lapply(decon$rwls_weights, function(w) quantile(w, probs = c(0, 0.01, 0.05, 0.5), na.rm = TRUE))
```

For details on Sobolev versus ridge penalties, `scaling = "noise_sd"`, and `rwls = "auto"`, see [Step 2](../medusa_step2_deconvolution/medusa_step2_deconvolution.qmd).

---

### 3. Steps 3 & 4: Motion-Scrubbing Shadows in Trial SEs and Shrunken Outcome Misuse {#sec-qc-step34}

![Healthy versus mis-specified trial epoching and panel assembly in Steps 3 and 4. **A:** Propagated trial-level standard error (`se_demixed`) across 16 feedback trials in Run 1. In an uncensored run (blue), interior trials share uniform precision (`se_demixed` $\approx 0.062$) with an expected uptick only on Trial 16 (`215.5 s`, whose causal HRF tail is truncated by scanner shutoff at `220 s`). When 3 frames on Trial 7's HRF peak are motion-scrubbed (red), `se_demixed` spikes selectively at Trial 7 (`0.076`) so downstream precision weights downweight it automatically; when 10 frames covering Trial 11's HRF are scrubbed, `min_bold_coverage` gates Trial 11 cleanly to `NA` (red dashed line). **B:** Entering `decon_demixed` + `precision_weight_cohort` in `mixed_by()` across 16 participants recovers the generating slope (`0.454` vs. truth `0.50`, blue), whereas mistakenly entering empirical-Bayes shrunken `decon_eb` as the outcome shrinks the estimated population slope nearly in half (`0.231`, red).](figures/03-qc-censor-shadow-and-eb.png){#fig-qc-step34 width="100%" fig-alt="Two-panel diagnostic for Steps 3 and 4 showing trial-by-trial se_demixed spikes and NA gating under motion scrubbing on the left, and group slope attenuation when shrunken decon_eb is entered as a mixed_by outcome on the right."}

**What to look for in @fig-qc-step34:**

- **Protective `se_demixed` spikes vs. run-wide degradation (Panel A):** Seeing isolated spikes in `panel$se_demixed` (like Trial 7) or run-boundary upticks (like Trial 16) is *not* a software bug—it is the propagated sandwich covariance $\Omega_{r,\tau}$ faithfully recording where censored frames or run-end truncation reduced effective BOLD observations inside that event's hemodynamic window. When `precision_weight_cohort` is passed to `mixed_by()`, Trial 7 receives lower inverse-variance weight automatically, and Trial 11 (`NA`) is omitted without shifting `event_index`. Intervention is only warranted when a run has so many censored frames that *most* trials sit at elevated `se_demixed` or `NA`.
- **Outcome vs. predictor column roles in Step 4 panels (Panel B):** Step 4 exports both unshrunken `decon_demixed` ($\widehat{z}_{ri} = \theta_{ri} + e_{ri}$) and empirical-Bayes shrunken `decon_eb` ($\tilde{z}_{ri} \approx \bar{z} + \kappa_{ri}(\widehat{z}_{ri} - \bar{z})$, where $\kappa_{ri} = \widehat{\tau}^2 / (\widehat{\tau}^2 + s_{ri}^2) < 1$). Entering `decon_eb` on the left-hand side of `mixed_by()` multiplies the true fixed-effect slope by $\bar{\kappa} < 1$ (`0.231` vs. `0.454` here), biasing population inference toward zero.

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# Audit per-run NA gating rate and high-SE tail in Step 3/4 panels
panel_dt <- data.table::as.data.table(epochs$panel)
panel_dt[, .(
  pct_gated_na = 100 * mean(is.na(decon_demixed)),
  median_se    = median(se_demixed, na.rm = TRUE),
  p95_se       = quantile(se_demixed, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)
), by = run]

# Always pair decon_demixed + precision_weight_cohort when neural activity is the outcome
group_models <- mixed_by(group_panel, outcomes = "decon_demixed",
                         rhs_model_formulae = ~ rpe_within + (1 + rpe_within || id) + (1 | id:run),
                         split_on = c("parcel", "evt_time"), weights = "precision_weight_cohort")
```

For full guidance on `min_bold_coverage`, `(T, O)` de-mixing, and column-role assignment, see [Step 3](../medusa_step3_epochs/medusa_step3_epochs.qmd) and [Step 4](../medusa_step4_parcel_panels/medusa_step4_parcel_panels.qmd).

---

### 4. Steps 5 & 6: Multilevel Centering/Random-Slope Pitfalls and Connectivity Shared Noise {#sec-qc-step56}

![Healthy versus mis-specified group inference (Step 5) and trial-level connectivity (Step 6). **A:** Across 36 participants (`16` target trials/person) where true within-person trial coupling is `+0.45` but between-person trait coupling is `-0.35` with participant slope SD `0.42`, decomposing `x_within + x_mean` with `(1 + x_within || id)` recovers `+0.434` (`df = 35`, blue). Entering uncentered `x_raw` conflates within- and between-person variance and flips the estimated slope to `-0.258` (red), while omitting the random slope `(1 | id)` understates uncertainty with pooled-trial degrees of freedom (`df = 573`, amber). **B:** Participant connectivity slopes (`ppi$subjects`, `term == "seed_c"`) across 16 participants where true seed-to-target neural coupling is `0.35` and shared cross-parcel measurement error is $r_{ST} = 0.55$. M-MOMS with `shared_error = "auto"` recovers `0.295` (blue); stripping `unit_error_cor` / `shared_noise_loading` (`shared_error = "zero"`) disattenuates shared noise up to `0.751` (red); naive OLS without measurement-error repair attenuates down to `0.178` (amber).](figures/04-qc-residual-ac1-and-mmoms.png){#fig-qc-step56 width="100%" fig-alt="Two-panel diagnostic for Steps 5 and 6 showing mixed-model centering sign-flip and random-slope CI narrowing on the left, and participant connectivity boxplots comparing M-MOMS auto shared error against stripped shared error and naive OLS on the right."}

**What to look for in @fig-qc-step56:**

- **Within/between conflation and inflated degrees of freedom in Step 5 (Panel A):** Any predictor that varies both across trials within a person (e.g., trial-by-trial RT, value, arousal) and in mean level across people (fast vs. slow responders, high vs. low baseline value) carries two distinct biological associations. Entering raw `x_raw` forces `lmer()` to estimate a precision-weighted blend of $\beta_{\text{within}}$ and $\beta_{\text{between}}$—which can attenuate or even reverse the sign of the trial effect (`-0.258` vs. `+0.45`). Equally important, inspect the `df` column of `coef_df_reml`: a within-person fixed effect tested across $S = 36$ participants should have Satterthwaite `df` near $S - 1$ (`35`), *never* in the hundreds (`573`), which signals that the random slope `(1 + x_within || id)` was omitted or collapsed to zero.
- **Asymmetric bias modes in Step 6 connectivity (Panel B):** When deconvolved seed activity moves to the *right-hand side* as a noisy predictor (`Target ~ Seed * Task`), two opposing biases act simultaneously: seed estimation variance $s_{S,i}^2$ *attenuates* naive OLS toward zero (`0.178`), while correlated scanner/physiological noise shared across parcels ($r_{ST} > 0$) *inflates* coupling. If you export `panel` to a plain `.csv` file without `shared_noise_loading` or the participant `unit_error_cor` matrix (forcing `shared_error = "zero"`), M-MOMS subtracts seed error variance in the denominator without subtracting shared error covariance in the numerator—magnifying shared noise (`0.751`). Passing the intact `subject_epochs` list (or preserving `shared_noise_loading` in tabular exports) allows `shared_error = "auto"` to correct both terms simultaneously (`0.295`).

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# Step 5 audit: check Satterthwaite df on within-person terms (should scale with N_subjects, not N_trials)
subset(group_models$coef_df_reml, term == "rpe_within")[, c("parcel", "evt_time", "estimate", "std.error", "df")]

# Step 6 audit: confirm r_shared_error is non-zero when expected and check convergence
ppi <- decon_connectivity_repair(
  subject_epochs, seed_region = "Seed", target_region = "Target",
  covariates = "x_within", shared_error = "auto", method = "mmoms"
)
summary(ppi$subjects[, c("r_shared_error", "alpha_final", "converged")])
```

For complete coverage of group trajectory modeling and M-MOMS connectivity repair, see [Step 5](../medusa_step5_group_models/medusa_step5_group_models.qmd) and [Step 6](../medusa_step6_connectivity/medusa_step6_connectivity.qmd).

<details>
<summary>Simulation Details & Reproduction</summary>

All four healthy-versus-pathological figure pairs and @tbl-qc-summary are generated from live `medusa` calls (`estimate_crossrun_hrf()`, `deconvolve_crossrun_hrf()`, `diagnose_crossrun_recovery()`, `decon_epoch_regression()`, `mixed_by()`, and `decon_connectivity_repair()`) with fixed seed `20261116`:

- **Pair 1 (Steps 0 & 1):** 3 runs $\times$ 140 volumes at `TR = 2.0 s`, 16 jittered feedback events/run with true lag-0 RPE slope `0.60`; compares `valid_rows` dummy masking (`1:3`) against physical truncation (`Y[-c(1:3), ]` with `time_offset = 0`) and onset-unit mis-specification (`on_sec / tr_slow`). Step 1 `rho` check simulates 36 parcels (`true rho` uniform on `[0.30, 0.62]`) with and without an unmodeled mid-run shim step + `0.008 Hz` drift.
- **Pair 2 (Step 2):** 3 runs $\times$ 180 volumes at `TR = 1.0 s`; compares `valid_rows` censoring + automatic GCV $\lambda_v$ + `rwls = "auto"` against `lambda = 8.0` and an uncensored `91 s` spike with `rwls = "none"`.
- **Pair 3 (Steps 3 & 4):** 3 runs $\times$ 220 volumes (`16` trials/run, Trial 16 at `215.5 s`), comparing uncensored `se_demixed` against partial peak scrubbing on Trial 7 (`3` frames) and full HRF scrubbing on Trial 11 (`10` frames); plus a 16-participant cohort comparing `decon_demixed` + `precision_weight_cohort` against shrunken `decon_eb` as outcome in `mixed_by()` (true slope `0.50`).
- **Pair 4 (Steps 5 & 6):** Step 5 simulates $S = 36$ participants (`16` target trials/person, $\beta_{\text{within}} = +0.45$, $\beta_{\text{between}} = -0.35$, random slope SD `0.42`). Step 6 simulates $S = 16$ participants (`80` trials/person, true seed-target slope `0.35`, shared cross-parcel error correlation $r_{ST} = 0.55$, trial SE `0.75`).
